term: moved by something (ὑπό τινος), by another, per accidens
resolution: Three different claims about a moved thing's mover. 'By something' (ὑπό τινος) allows the thing itself; 'by another' (ὑπʼ ἄλλου, `MovedByAnother`) requires a distinct mover; a per accidens mover (`MovesPerAccidensIn`) is a mover only in a way. `MovesIn` is always per se moving, in the sense of DEF-MOTION-AS-REDUCTION. The literal reading of Physics VIII.4 (STMT-EVERY-MOVED-THING-MOVED-PER-SE-OR-PER-ACCIDENS) keeps the per accidens disjunct; only the generator reading (STMT-PASSIVE-NATURAL-MOTION-BY-GENERATOR) yields a per se mover, and result ARIST-PHYS-VIII-4-EVERY-MOVED-PER-SE-OR-PER-ACCIDENS shows the literal reading does not yield STMT-NOTHING-REDUCED-TO-ACT-EXCEPT-BY-A-MOVER. STMT-EVERY-MOVED-THING-HAS-SOME-MOVER is respect-free 'by something'; it is not the prima via's respect-indexed premise and is not identified with it.
